Add priors to a four-component stochastic frontier model

Source: R/add_priors.sfmodel4.R
add_priors.sfmodel4_exp.Rd

Attaches the prior specification to a model object produced by create_sfmodel4_exp or create_sfmodel4_hn.

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel4_exp'
add_priors(
  object,
  coef = list(mu = 0, v_i = 0.01),
  sigma = list(shape = 0.01, rate = 0.01),
  sigma_mu = list(shape = 0.01, rate = 0.01),
  lambda_eta = list(r_star = 0.9, shape = 1),
  lambda_u = list(r_star = 0.9, shape = 1),
  varsel = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel4_hn'
add_priors(
  object,
  coef = list(mu = 0, v_i = 0.01),
  sigma = list(shape = 0.01, rate = 0.01),
  sigma_mu = list(shape = 0.01, rate = 0.01),
  sigma_eta = list(r_star = 0.9, shape = 2.5),
  sigma_u = list(r_star = 0.9, shape = 2.5),
  varsel = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

an object of class "sfmodel4_exp" or "sfmodel4_hn".

coef

a named list of prior specifications for the frontier coefficients, with elements mu, the prior mean, and v_i, the prior precision.

sigma

a named list of prior specifications for the error precision, with elements shape and rate.

sigma_mu

a named list of prior specifications for the precision of the unit effect, with elements shape and rate.

lambda_eta

a named list for the rate of the exponential distribution of persistent inefficiency, with elements r_star and shape.

lambda_u

a named list for the rate of the exponential distribution of transient inefficiency, with elements r_star and shape.

varsel

a named list of prior specifications for the variable selection algorithm. Required if the model was created with a varsel algorithm, and not allowed otherwise. It takes the same elements as in add_priors for the two-component models, and applies to the frontier coefficients only.

...

unused, for compatibility with the generic.

sigma_eta

a named list for the scale of the half-normal distribution of persistent inefficiency, with elements r_star and shape.

sigma_u

a named list for the scale of the half-normal distribution of transient inefficiency, with elements r_star and shape.

Value

The model object with the element priors attached.

Details

The blocks for the frontier coefficients and the error precision are those of add_priors for the two-component models. Two further blocks are needed here.

The unit effect \(\mu_i \sim N(0, \sigma_\mu^2)\) takes a gamma prior on its precision. With few units the posterior for \(\sigma_\mu\) is sensitive to that choice, and the vague default is not a neutral one in the sense that Gelman (2006) discusses; a sensitivity check is worth running before reading much into the split between \(\mu_i\) and \(\eta_i\).

The two one-sided terms are elicited separately, each from its own prior median efficiency, exactly as in the two-component case. Note that the anchors apply per component: with r_star = 0.9 for each, the prior median of the overall efficiency \(\exp(-\eta_i - u_{it})\) is near 0.81 rather than 0.9. The default of 0.9 is chosen with that in mind.

References

Gelman, A. (2006). Prior distributions for variance parameters in hierarchical models. Bayesian Analysis, 1(3), 515–534.

See also

add_priors for the two-component models.

Examples

set.seed(1234)
d <- sim_sf4(n = 60, n_time = 8, beta = c(1, 0.5, 0.3))

model <- create_sfmodel4_exp(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, id = "id",
                             iterations = 500, burnin = 200)
model <- add_priors(model,
                    lambda_eta = list(r_star = 0.95),
                    lambda_u = list(r_star = 0.9))
model$priors$r_star
#> persistent  transient 
#>       0.95       0.90
